features.description: When Markie's embedded terminal is enabled, a new shell starts in the current document folder and exposes MARKIE_FILE, MARKIE_DIR, and MARKIE_WORKSPACE for the active document.
steps: Open a markdown file in Markie with the terminal feature enabled in a development run.
Create a new embedded terminal session.
Run `pwd` and confirm it starts in the active document's folder.
Run `printf '%s\n' "$MARKIE_FILE" "$MARKIE_DIR" "$MARKIE_WORKSPACE"` and confirm the values match the active document and workspace.
Run the focused terminal regression test plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm test -- electron/terminal.test.ts` passed with 5 tests, including terminal Markie context regression. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-015021-post-f001.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Implemented env/cwd injection only. The terminal UI remains hidden by `TERMINAL_ENABLED = false`, so the user journey was verified via the focused Electron terminal regression instead of manual UI driving.

features.description: When the active document changes, future embedded terminal sessions receive updated Markie context instead of stale document paths.
steps: Open document A, then open document B in the same Markie session.
Create a new embedded terminal session after document B becomes active.
Confirm MARKIE_FILE and MARKIE_DIR point at document B, not document A.
Run the focused terminal regression test plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm test -- electron/terminal.test.ts` passed with 6 tests, including the document A to document B future-shell context regression. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-automated-f002-post.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Depends on F-001. Verified future shells pick up the newly active document context. Existing shells are intentionally not re-injected.

features.description: A safe preflight command verifies release prerequisites without signing, notarizing, uploading, or touching production services.
steps: Run the documented release preflight command on a clean checkout without release credentials.
Confirm it checks package metadata, required local files, and build/test prerequisites.
Confirm it exits before any publish, notarize, upload, deploy, or credentialed network action.
Run `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm test -- electron/release-preflight.test.ts` passed 3 tests. `npm run release:preflight > .autoloop/runs/release-preflight-20260628-035123.log 2>&1` passed metadata, required-file, renderer/Electron, MCP, server, lint, and static build checks, ending before credentialed release actions. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-035139-post-f003.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Added `npm run release:preflight` as a local-only DX gate. Actual signing, notarization, upload, publish, deploy, and credentialed release actions remain human checkpoints.

features.description: The MCP server has a regression journey proving allowed markdown writes remain fenced to safe local markdown paths.
steps: Run the MCP test suite and identify the current filesystem guard coverage.
Add a user-observable MCP write/read regression that writes an allowed markdown file under a temporary safe home and reads it back.
Confirm symlink escape and unsafe extension cases still fail.
Run `node --test mcp/lib.test.mjs` and `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Do not widen the MCP public API shape in this task.

features.description: A real-user comments regression verifies thread creation, reply, resolve, reopen, and anchor survival using the existing verifier scripts.
steps: Run the existing comments verification scripts against the local dev server setup they document.
If setup gaps prevent the journey, add the smallest script/docs fix needed for repeatable local verification.
Confirm the journey covers create, reply, resolve, reopen, and anchor survival after an edit above the selection.
Run the focused comments verifier plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Do not change comments product UX unless a failing verification requires a narrow bugfix.
